extracted.intended_audience: IB Diploma Programme English A: Language and Literature HL students, teachers and examiners
extracted.subtask_short: IB English A HL essay assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment criteria for the HL essay in IB English A: Language and Literature, defining what examiners look for across Knowledge/Understanding, Analysis/Evaluation, Coherence/Organisation and Language with five-level performance descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion A: Knowledge, understanding and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the essay show knowledge and understanding of the work or body of work? To what extent are interpretations drawn from the work or body of work to explore the topic? To what extent are interpretations supported by relevant references to the work or body of work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: The essay shows little knowledge and understanding of the work or body of work. Interpretations are rarely relevant to the topic and rarely supported by references to the work or body of work.
Level 2: The essay shows some knowledge and understanding of the work or body of work. Interpretations are somewhat relevant to the topic and sometimes supported by references to work or body of work.
Level 3: The essay shows adequate knowledge and understanding of the work or body of work. Interpretations are generally relevant to the topic and generally supported by references to the work or body of work.
Level 4: The essay shows a good knowledge and understanding of the work or body of work. Interpretations are very relevant to the topic and often supported by appropriate references to the work or body of work.
Level 5: The essay shows perceptive knowledge and understanding of the work or body of work. Interpretations are consistently relevant to the topic and effectively supported by convincing references to the work or body of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion B: Analysis and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the essay show analysis and evaluation of how the author uses stylistic and structural features to construct meaning on the topic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: The essay shows little analysis and evaluation of how the author uses stylistic and structural features to construct meaning on the topic.
Level 2: The essay shows some analysis and evaluation of how the author uses stylistic and structural features to construct meaning on the topic.
Level 3: The essay shows adequate analysis and evaluation of how the author uses stylistic and structural features to construct meaning on the topic.
Level 4: The essay shows good analysis and evaluation of how the author uses stylistic and structural features to construct meaning on the topic.
Level 5: The essay shows insightful analysis and evaluation of how the author uses stylistic and structural features to construct meaning on the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion C: Coherence, focus and organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the essay show coherence, focus and organisation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: The essay shows little coherence, focus and organisation.
Level 2: The essay shows some coherence, focus and organisation.
Level 3: The essay shows adequate coherence, focus and organisation.
Level 4: The essay shows good coherence, focus and organisation.
Level 5: The essay shows effective coherence, focus and organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion D: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the student’s use of vocabulary, tone, syntax, style and terminology accurate, varied and effective?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Level 1: The student’s use of vocabulary, tone, syntax, style and terminology is rarely accurate, varied and effective.
Level 2: The student’s use of vocabulary, tone, syntax, style and terminology is sometimes accurate, varied and effective.
Level 3: The student’s use of vocabulary, tone, syntax, style and terminology is generally accurate, varied and effective.
Level 4: The student’s use of vocabulary, tone, syntax, style and terminology is frequently accurate, varied and effective.
Level 5: The student’s use of vocabulary, tone, syntax, style and terminology is convincingly accurate, varied and effective.
